primaryContext.title: Ingrid opens a new dimension into Street Fighter 6 on May 28!
primaryContext.archiveEvidence: The complete official Steam announcement body and article identity were archived locally from Capcom’s announcement feed.
primaryContext.note: Capcom describes up to four Sun Crests, light-Sun-Flare storage/hold, up to two-Crest enhancement for heavy/OD Sun Flare, Solar Burst, Sun Shot, Sun Rise and Vanishing Sun. Level-2 strength changes rain placement and held Crest use increases the rain. Actual source inputs, starting HUD and results govern each excerpt. No current-patch gameplay certification is inferred.

interpretationDecisions.decision: Medium-Sun-Rise knockdown and the Rush-cancel/heavy-Rise/light-Flare-storage knockdown are separate prerequisites. Listed setup inputs/costs begin afterward. The printed +38/+25/+5/+22 readings are source-reported advantage, not invented numerical wait instructions. Intentional cr.LK whiff is explicit in compact/copy notation.

Cyan/light, yellow/medium and red/heavy input glyphs and performed animation govern strength. The shimmy uses actual st.HK before the medium target chain. The crouching-medium target-chain card requires crouching Ryu; normal-HK light links and Counter-Hit-HK medium links are separate recorded conditions.

Conditions state the visible initial Crests and the observed spend/refill. Heavy/OD Sun Flare uses the recorded enhancement; an intermediate one-Crest HUD during a two-Crest sequence is not mistaken for a one-Crest route. Light Sun Flare storage after knockdown is not described as a connecting attack. Heavy Sun Rise already leaves Ingrid airborne for j.MP; no separate jump input is performed. Ingrid then lands before the one-Crest grounded OD Sun Flare, followed by light-Flare refill.

Heavy versus light punch and the actual hold are explicit. The source begins with two Crests for the heavy-rain branches, one or two for the distinct light-rain back throws; its later light Sun Flare refills the stock used by OD Sun Flare. Heavy 236HP projectiles are Sun Shot, not Sun Rise kicks. No universal gap/reversal-safety claim is inferred.

Two Vesper grounded back-heavy jump interceptions get Anti-air; neither claims a reaction test. Joe’s opening jab/counter-DI exchanges are responses and keep the actual opening action. Own blocked DI against an already-Burnout near-corner Ryu causes wall stun, distinct from counter-DI and ordinary wall crush; it begins Midscreen and has observed Corner carry.
Only the light-confirm route that visibly spends both Rush cancels into Burnout and Level 3 receives Cash-out. Level-2 cover and other Super use alone do not imply the goal.
The printed OD/Rush/delayed-Flare/Level-1 candidate is excluded because its intermediate Crest interpretation is unresolved; no inferred Level-1 stock gain is authored.

remainingGaps: Most Vesper punish, Rush, Sun-Flare, Super and corner choices remain unextracted.
Joe still offers air-OD/corner, multiple Super/resource, forward-heavy, raw-Rush and counter-DI alternatives; these intervals remain explicitly unprocessed.
The Level-1 Crest/state ambiguity and printed “any” ender require clearer follow-up evidence before extraction.
No current-patch gameplay certification is claimed.
